prompt: Solve for $x$: $\log_2(x) + \log_2(x - 6) = 4$. Give the one answer that works.
hint: Adding logs with the same base means multiplying inside, so combine them into one log first.

hints.text: Adding logs with the same base means multiplying inside, so combine them into one log first.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: $\log_2(x) + \log_2(2) = 3$ becomes $\log_2(2x) = 3$, so $2x = 8$ and $x = 4$. Same move — combine, then rewrite as a power.
The combined equation $\log_2\big(x(x-6)\big) = 4$ means $x(x - 6) = 2^4 = 16$, so $x^2 - 6x - 16 = 0$. Factor this and test each solution in the original logs.
It factors as $(x - 8)(x + 2) = 0$, giving $x = 8$ or $x = -2$. Since $\log_2(-2)$ is impossible, the answer is $x = 8$.

explanation: Combine the two logs with the product rule: $\log_2\big(x(x-6)\big) = 4$.
Rewrite the log equation as a power: $x(x - 6) = 2^4 = 16$, which rearranges to $x^2 - 6x - 16 = 0$.
Factoring gives $(x - 8)(x + 2) = 0$. The value $x = -2$ fails because a log cannot take a negative input, so the only answer is $x = 8$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check both answers in the original
steps: Try $x = -2$: the very first term is $\log_2(-2)$, and no power of $2$ is negative.
So $x = -2$ is thrown out and $x = 8$ stands.

alternativeExplanations.title: Fence off the illegal values first
steps: Before solving, note $x > 0$ AND $x - 6 > 0$, so $x$ must be bigger than $6$.
